notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Authored by claude-opus-5-5 (a model and not a human; phase-4 agent p4-unity, run p4-unity-20261105) under the user's decision of 2026-11-05 (user-decisions-20261105.json, decision 3): Claude authors, a Claude Sonnet model reviews before merge; reviewed_by stays null. Nothing of Unity, ROS, MoveIt, rosbridge or the pose model was installed or run. SUPERSEDES the code-less blocked record (HELPER_MISSING, NEEDS_ARTIFACTS; the original RESULT.json is kept in work/handoff-runs/claude-20261104/development/p4-unity/moved-aside/snapshot-5-package/). ROUTE DECISION (the triage's three needs). (1) Owning trajectory execution: no route exists. Unity executes the plans in a coroutine that only the response to its own MoverService request starts (PoseEstimationDemoProject/Assets/TutorialAssets/Scripts/TrajectoryPlanner.cs:255-264, 288-333); the Unity scripts send two service requests and subscribe to no topic and implement no service, so neither a ROS-TCP profile nor a helper can command, own or stop the arm; a ROS-TCP client would reach the same two ROS services the endpoint routes (ROS/src/ur3_moveit/scripts/server_endpoint.py:15-19) as rosbridge does. The arm and gripper are NOT COVERED; their only stop is the Unity editor. (2) Image requests as artifacts: not built. The image exists only inside Unity's button handler and its own request (TrajectoryPlanner.cs:105-120, 168-176); no ROS topic carries it, the SDK's artifacts are endpoint outputs, and a client-supplied image route would be new protocol surface without a producer in this deployment that would also have to reproduce Unity's request layout (TrajectoryPlanner.cs:170-173 passes width and height in the height and width slots with step 4, and pose_estimation_script.py:32-35 swaps them back and flips the rows). The pose service stays NOT COVERED (NEEDS_ARTIFACTS for it is listed as found, not fixed). (3) Submodules: two facts cite moveit_msgs (gitlink 1d6168c0) and ros_tcp_endpoint (gitlink c56f5586), read at their gitlinks (G1.SUBMODULE_SOURCE; BSD and Apache 2.0 by their package.xml, not on the card). SCOPE: the smallest honest route is the existing RosDriver over rosbridge (installed by docker/Dockerfile:5) and no SDK change: x-cap.unity-technologies.pick_place_plan.v1 calls /ur3_moveit (ur3_moveit/MoverService, mover.py:141, type import :19) with the six start angles in degrees (mover.py:66-73 converts them) and the pick and place poses, and returns the five plans' joint names and points (pre grasp, grasp, pick up, place, post place; mover.py:75-110); output executed is always false. Declared operation read, verb read, exclusive: the callback plans and returns (mover.py:35-46, 61-110); its state changes are the table box it re-adds to MoveIt's planning scene after a 2 s sleep and the module-global MoveGroupCommander it replaces (mover.py:112-126). A planning call is answered to this endpoint, never to Unity, so it starts nothing. DISCLOSED HAZARD: the node keeps its MoveGroupCommander in a module global that every call replaces (mover.py:112-116) and rospy serves different clients in parallel, so a call that overlaps Unity's own planning call can mix this package's start state or targets into the plan Unity then executes in its simulation; the action description, facts.md and the fidelity gaps say to plan only while the scene is not planning. STOP: only an observational command, so the software latch is the whole safety path; tests show the e-stop completes at once with a plan in flight (that plan is not completed), refuses later plans and that a second call is not sent while one is pending. RISK: R1, the card's floor; by the hazard table the package is R0 (it commands no arm). A Unity simulation is R0 unless it commands a real arm: here no arm, simulated or real, is commanded by the package, and the pipeline has no real arm (MoveIt's configured /follow_joint_trajectory controller, config/ros_controllers.yaml:1-11, is served by no node of pose_est.launch, and the callback never executes). FAKE: a recording rosbridge transport (fake.py) with placeholder joint configurations, point counts and spacing; it models the five-plan order, the chaining of each plan's start to the previous plan's end, the degree-to-radian start and failed calls. test_driver.py: the gate and 14 repository cases (request leaves, plan order and chaining, failed plan, short, foreign-joint and truncated-point answers (OUTPUT_INVALID), malformed input refused before the service, published contract and manifest, serialisation, the e-stop with and without a plan in flight); 10 of 10 package mutants killed (work/handoff-runs/claude-20261104/development/p4-unity/scripts/package_mutants.py). Live route (never run): the documented ROS side (Documentation/4_pick_and_place.md:197-209) plus an operator-run rosbridge, through simulation_deployment.
